expected_what.value: New-hire access requests are submitted by the manager via a ServiceNow form, checked by IT Security against a standard role-based access profile, and provisioned in Active Directory / target application groups.

expected_who.value: Requestor: the new hire's manager. Reviewer/provisioner: an IT Security Analyst plus one colleague in IT Security.

expected_when.value: Continuously, triggered by HR's new-starter notification (not on a fixed schedule); target of 2 business days from the start date.

expected_why.value: To prevent over-provisioning or access outside the new hire's role - i.e. to stop a manager's request being granted as-is without an independent check against the role's standard profile.

expected_where.value: ServiceNow (request form, approval, provisioning ticket in one record) and Active Directory (account and application group provisioning).

expected_how.value: Manager submits a ServiceNow access request; IT Security compares it to the standard role-based access profile; the analyst creates the AD account from a role-based template, assigns the approved application groups, and attaches a screenshot of the final group membership to the ticket.

source.excerpt: their manager submits an access request form through the ServiceNow portal
I do, along with one of my colleagues in IT Security
triggered every time HR notifies us of a new starter
this is our way of preventing over-provisioning or granting access outside someone's role
I create the account in Active Directory using our standard role-based templates

expected_design_rationale: All six attributes are clearly established from a single consistent account. The control has an independent reviewer (IT Security, distinct from the requesting manager), a defined criterion (standard role-based profile), a target timeframe, a stated rationale tied directly to the risk, and retained evidence (ServiceNow record plus a screenshot of resulting access). Relevant to the risk and aligned with the stated control objective.

expected_risk_objective_control_alignmen.rationale: The control as described directly achieves the stated objective: manager-initiated requests are independently checked against a role-based profile before provisioning, which is exactly the mechanism the objective calls for.

reviewer_notes: This is the pilot's 'clean' baseline case: a single fluent account, no contradictions, covers all six attributes with a stated rationale distinct from a generic 'best practice' answer. Used to test that AssureAI reaches ALIGNED/PASS conclusions with SUPPORTED citations when the evidence genuinely supports it - not just that it can hedge or flag issues.
